strengths: Addresses a relevant problem: retaining information beyond a transformer's context in offline RL. Evaluation covers visual and vector observations, memory tasks, Atari, and MuJoCo.
The strongest evidence is the T-Maze extrapolation result: after training on lengths up to 150, MRV achieves 0.90 ± 0.07 success at length 900, versus 0.61 ± 0.07 without MRV (Table 3).
Memory perturbations, component ablations, curriculum comparisons, and five MRV variants provide useful evidence about the mechanism's contribution.
Reports substantial improvements on Qbert and Breakout and lower GPU memory usage. Environment descriptions, training details, and a code link support reproducibility.
weaknesses: The architectural novelty is limited: RATE combines Decision Transformer tokenization, Recurrent Memory Transformer tokens, Transformer-XL caching, and standard cross-attention. The paper needs stronger evidence that this combination offers a meaningful advance over established memory architectures.

The main memory-task baseline is fixed-context Decision Transformer, whose failure after losing access to the cue is expected. Despite useful component ablations, comparisons with competitive recurrent policies and state-space models on these tasks are missing. GRU/LSTM variants of the memory valve do not replace comparisons against complete recurrent agents.

Section 3 states both that updated memory embeddings are detached and that gradients flow through them into previous segments. These statements are incompatible as written. Because later action losses provide the learning signal for MRV, this ambiguity concerns an essential part of the training algorithm.

MuJoCo improvements are confounded by an additional inference change: Appendix C resets the target return at every segment, while baseline scores are imported from prior papers. DT with the same reset and RATE without it are needed to isolate the architecture's contribution. Also, RATE has the highest reported mean in only 2/9 tasks in Table 2, whereas Appendix C claims the best metrics in 5/9.

The ViZDoom memory interpretation requires clarification. Appendix A says rewards are withheld to prevent revealing the target color, but Section 3 supplies return-to-go tokens updated using observed rewards. Unless an undocumented exception applies, consecutive tokens reveal reward feedback, providing an alternative source of color information and weakening attribution to retention of the initial pillar.

The parameter-overhead calculation omits the learned MRV query, key, value, and output projections. Consequently, the claimed overhead of approximately 1,000 parameters and the associated capacity comparison are not supported by the architecture as specified.
